iustitia.name: Iustitia
iustitia.summary: A legal practice system that tracks court publications and deadlines so the lawyer doesn't have to.
iustitia.description: Small firms miss deadlines because somebody has to read the official gazette every single day. Iustitia does that reading on its own: it pulls publications from the CNJ, classifies each one with AI, and only then hands it to a person to decide. Human review is mandatory, because misreading a deadline costs far too much to leave to a model unchecked. Underneath it's a modular monolith in .NET, with Clean Architecture, CQRS and multi-tenancy on PostgreSQL.

sigis.name: SIGIS
sigis.summary: A platform for tracking care for people with autism across public services in Crateús, Brazil.
sigis.description: Caring for someone with autism through public services means dealing with three departments that don't talk to each other: health, education and social services. Each one holds a piece of the story and nobody sees the whole. SIGIS pulls those pieces into a single view. I built it alone during a hackathon run by Banco do Nordeste with UFC and the Crateús city government, under the name Last Soldier, and it placed fourth.

filesharing.name: FileSharing
filesharing.summary: File sharing through private links that expire after 24 hours.
filesharing.description: It came out of a simple annoyance: sending someone a large file without leaning on personal cloud storage or leaving it sitting there forever. Uploads go straight to a private S3 bucket, the link is unguessable, and it expires in 24 hours. JWT for auth, live progress over SignalR, and Clean Architecture on ASP.NET Core.
